alterations.description: Words of Chandran 'Enalcku Ore Voarthaiyil Sorgavasalai Ksatlvitteerkal'.
Karpakan playing to his friends 'We shall all enjoy Pooncholayal together' (Ellarumaai Shorndhu Pooncholayal Raapom).
All the picture and dialogue of Suryakantan asking for a kiss from Angayarkanni before he goes, in Reels 8, 10.
Portion of the dialogue between Solai and Karumbu where she asks whether he could carry a Kujai and his reply that he cannot but he will be willing to do so for her.

In Suryakantan’s speech: description of fraudulent persons who he says 'walk with thin land in daylight disguise, who dally with women at night and speak philosophy in the morning, who preach the path of truth to the people of the nobloland and themselves adopt crooked methods, who plan to cut throats while speaking sweet words, the cheats, the puns humbugs.' (Mannavaa Iunatlle...indhu Asakaya Suran) (Dialogue only); the description of treason as clear writing on the wall, the casting of mud on the civilisation of the land by distinguishing among Gods. In the name of high devotion; the creation of ills in the name of sacrifice, under the cloak of common good. (Karaikadantlia Baktld...Therlavlllaya Unakku); the statement that it is clear there is a gang of conspirators who cut the throat while claiming kinship, and it is also clear who they are (Uravoadi Kazhutharakkum...Therikfrf. thu); the statement that in the herd of deer a foals walking. (Polllmaan Nadaipodukirathu). (Dialogue only).

Speech of Chandran saving: 'You play chess with the native of the land for getting you are a foreigner — you a foreigner interfere in local affairs. Tomorrow you will send an army here in the name of security, national welfare etc.' But the people of this land are not fools to be cheated. They will ask why, wherefore and how. (Vandhavun Naam....Aaralchivum Cheivaarkal); 'I am a criminal, so is my family and this land which was ruined by its own; it received those who came for livelihood, toiled for them and fed and fattened them. (Naan Kuttrawali....Engal ivuttmm); It is our crime that we look on after the ruin of the land and its culture and tolerate the outsider settling here; that we received innocently the disguised also, and did not nip them in the bud; that we allowed the refugee also to roam this fairland; that you are of this tribe and interfere in local affairs. (Naadu Nalivathal Paarthum Alht Kovalamaana Kuttram)'.
Suryakantan saying 'According to the political leader, the cause of famine is the fraud in the heart of the rulers of the land,' (dialogue only).

Chandran saying: 'There is a greedy gang who strive for prizes, for enriching themselves by short cuts, who split people and divide the spoils. (Aanaa Adhu....Koor Podukindra Inam); He does not belong to the crowd who repay by ingratitude, the base who commit crimes, who kick down the ladder by which they climbed (Cheinandri Kollum....Shorndhavnmialla Naan) (dialogue only); Addressing Karpaka Mannan, 'Having come as a foreigner and spoken in a wounding manner, you roused self-respect and made volleys of raging minds; you helped to rouse sleeping lions — for having rendered this service, without knowing it, a special gratitude is due (Karpaka Mannare! Nandii)'.

Picture and dialogue of the Guru solemnising what he calls the Gandharva form of marriage, upto and including his blessing the couple and saying that he will send (Jliandum to the bed-room that night and it may be spent as a happy night by them.

Chandran saying 'Dogs the cry of revenge make your nerves shiver?' (Pazhikku-p-pazhl Nodunga Voikiratha?); This is the revolt of the son who thirsts for revenge against the leader of the land-hungry crowd that deprived the father of his kingdom. (Naanayamakka Vazhndha....Maindhanlu Mansvozhu hi); The passage between Marthandan and Chandran 'You will hang...the gallows are a swing for the brave man. Revenge is my ideal — Blood for Wood' (Thooku Mcdoyil Tudlppai....Ratthathirku Rattbam); Chandran telling Guru 'I am doing what old classics say — from before the age of rocks — trample underfoot the vermin who wound the hearts of the Tamil people, establish Dharma when injustice rears the head. Hence I took up the sword. (Kal Thondri Man thondrum Kaalathimnun....Nenjuruthl Kondon) — (dialogue only); Chandran offering to light single handed all the soldiers, Marthandan ordering hanging, and Suryakantan describing the types of people for whom the hanging would be a lesson and a threat (Aanal Tliooku Medayil Vendaam....Naadu Rhozhikkattum).
Strangling of Angayarkanni by Suryakantan, including his facial reactions and the sound of panting.
When Karumbu is chastised, delete Roall telling him 'do not interfere in local affairs' (Dl Noattu Vivakarathile Thalai Neetuvlyat).

Malayaman saying: 'Let there be war. Let swords dance. Bows and spears kill enemies, Martandan’s family be destroyed. Let the land be freed, the people crown you king' (Bor Nodakkattum .. V ndi Cnootattum); Son, these are good days for the land. On the sacrificial altar the fire of hate will rise, it will be fanned by the spirits of the dead; it will destroy the family, and race of Martaiuh. Long live Malanad and its people (Makano I Vnzhka Malainadavor).
